findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. FIRST REPEAT- The dish table to the right of the dish machine is observed to have an accumulation of soil residue in the caulking and needs to be re-sealed. 
2. The holes in the wall to the right of the dish machine need to be sealed. 
3. The handwashing sink in the women’s bathroom that is on the right side of the building is observed to have the sealing separated from the wall. Ensure that this is re-sealed. 
4. There is frost accumulation on the fans of the walk-in freezer. Ensure that the issue causing the frost accumulation is repaired. 

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: There was an open container of Barbecue sauce that was observed to be on a table in the kitchen and not in refrigeration. This sauce states to “Refrigerate after opening”. CORRECTED- The PIC discarded the Barbecue sauce and was educated to read labels of sauces. Ensure that food items that are Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) foods are held at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
The following equipment is observed to be in need of repair: 

1. There is a table that has pans holding it up. The PIC stated that the end of the table needs repaired. Ensure that this is repaired. 
2. The dish table to the right of the dish machine is observed to have an accumulation of soil residue in the caulking and needs re-sealed. 
3. The handle of the pizza preparation cooler is observed to be broken and is in need of being replaced. 

Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair and that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The small fan in the dish area. CORRECTED- The PIC removed it to be cleaned. 
2. The walk-in cooler fan covers. 
3. The bottom shelf holding sauces and plates across from the pizza oven on the cook-line. There is observed to be an accumulation of dust and soil residue on it. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There were raw shell eggs observed to be above containers of taco meat that had been cooked and cooled and other various food items. CORRECTED- These eggs were moved onto the shelf that holds other raw fish. Storage order was discussed with the PIC and another handout on storage order was provided. Ensure that food is protected from cross contamination during storage, holding, preparation, and display.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The top of the inside of the ice machine was observed to have slight soil residue accumulation. CORRECTED- This was cleaned during the inspection by the PIC. Ensure that this is cleaned regularly. Food contact surfaces should be clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment:
There were multiple single-service articles that were not being displayed correctly throughout the kitchen, including, but not limited to, the following: 

1. The to-go containers above the cook line. 
2. The plastic boats with parchment paper in them above the cook line. 
3. The bowls with parchment paper in them above the fryer area. 
4. The plates by the soup station. 

All single-service articles and utensils need to be inverted or stored directly under a shelf to protect them from contamination. This was discussed with the PIC.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The gasket of the pizza preparation cooler is observed to be in need of cleaning due to an accumulation of soil residue. 
2. The dish shelves next to the dish machine are observed to have soil accumulation and are in need of cleaning. 
3. The air vent above the dish area is observed to have an accumulation of dust and is in need of cleaning. 
4. The floor under the grills along the cook line in the kitchen. There is an accumulation of debris and soil residue. 
5. The bottom shelf of the table along the cook line in the kitchen. 
6. The wall behind the grills along the cook line in the kitchen. 
7. The floor of the walk-in freezer. It was discussed with the PIC to scrape off the built-up soil residue on the floor. 

Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to maintain them clean.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
4-501.11: There are a few gaskets on the doors of prep coolers that are falling off and need replaced or repaired. Ensure that all equipment is maintained in good repair. 

(B) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (B) EQUIPMENT components such as doors, seals, hinges, fasteners, and kick plates shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted in accordance with manufacturer's specifications.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The floor of the walk-in cooler and the floor under the dish machine were both observed to be in need of cleaning. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Ensure that these areas are cleaned and maintained cleaned. 

(A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Paper towel dispensers at both the front kitchen handsink and at the bar handsink were empty. CORRECTED- Employees refilled both paper towel dispensers. Ensure paper towels are available at all handwashing sinks.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
An employee’s medication (Victoza) was observed stored on the top shelf of the salad prep cooler, above dishes and individually-packaged applesauces. CORRECTED- Medication was placed in a pan and moved to proper storage. Store employee medications below and away from foods for service and food contact surfaces.
7-207.11: (A) Only medicines for health of EMPLOYEES shall be allowed in ESTABLISHMENT. (B) Medicines shall be labeled and located to prevent contamination to FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES. [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1) Both kitchen handwashing sinks are separating from the walls. Re-caulk both handsinks to the walls.
2) There is a hole in the wall below the back handsink. Seal/patch the hole so the wall is smooth and easily cleanable.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
PIC present does not have a current allergen training certificate. Ensure all CFMs complete ANSI-approved allergen training. Keep certificates on file for review during inspections.
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Items were observed in the hand sinks on the cook line and at the bar. Ensure hand washing sinks are used for only hand washing and are accessible for employees. The items were moved during the inspection. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The floors under the cook line, especially under the grill and near fryers are soiled with grease and food debris. Ensure physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary so they are maintained clean.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Some shelving in the walk in cooler was observed soiled with dust and other debris. Ensure shelving is cleaned at a frequency to prevent soil residue accumulation. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 4-601.11: (A) Observed baffle of ice machine to be soiled with debris. Baffle was cleaned during inspection. EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment: 6-501.110: (A) Observed employee cell phone located on shelf above prep cooler in kitchen.  Phone was removed.  Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D)  (C) Observed cookware lids and other cooking equipment stored in containers that were soiled with food debris. Equipment, Utensils, Linens and Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D).

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11  (Pf) Observed food employee filling a bowl with water at the handsink in the kitchen. Hand washing sink must be used for handwashing only. Reference 5-205.11.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: PA-100-0367 - All certified food managers working in a restaurant must complete additional allergen training using an approved allergen awareness training program.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
Employee beverage noted stored with and above clean utensils on preparation table located across from the hand sink in the kitchen area. 
->Please store employee drinks in a manner to prevent contamination from food, food prep ration areas, and clean utensils. Provide a lid and straw for beverage cups. Reference 2-401.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Employee cell phone observed stored on cutting board located on preparation table at East end of cookline. Discussed importance of storing cell phones away from food, food preparation areas, or clean utensils with employees. 

->Food contact surfaces must be protected from potential contamination.  Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Spray bottle of disinfectant noted stored on shelf above clean drainboard of chlorine dish machine.

-> Toxic materials must be stored so that they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens or single-service articles. Employee moved materials to separated storage. Reference 7-201.11.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
Observed ribeye steaks sitting on top shelf in center island preparation table. Staff indicated steaks were in the thawing process. Discussed thawing items under refrigeration. 
Bags of raw chicken noted thawing under running water in 3 compartment sink. Pan used for process noted small and chicken was observed hanging over edges of pan and not submerged in water. 
Observed raw salmon in vacuum sealed bags located in 6 pullout drawer cooler. Staff indicated salmon is thawed in vacuum sealed bags and then opened prior to cooking. 

->Thawing foods must be thawed: Under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41°F or less; or completely submerged under running at a water temperature of 70°F or below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow.  Reference 3-501.13.
->Frozen fish is thawing while still wrapped in reduced oxygen packaging (ROP). Packaging must be removed from fish in ROP prior to thawing under refrigeration or running water. Reference 3-501.13.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Handle of ice scoop observed touching ice in ice machine behind bar. 

->Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Door gasket seal on bottom right drawer of 6 door cooler noted cracked and in disrepair. 

->Replace the damaged or missing gaskets so the cooler can hold food at the proper temperature. Reference 4-501.11.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Interior of microwave found soiled with food debris located in promixity of steam wells in kitchen area. 

->Thoroughly clean all cooking equipment and pans. Reference 4-601.11(B) and (C).

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12 (A) Current manager has an expired CFM. Manager with CFM arrived during inspection. Present manager with lapsed CFM is enrolled in Febryary class. The person in charge shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114 Observed the sanitzing concentration of quat ammonia in sani-bucket to be at 100ppm. Bucket was emptied and filled with approved bleach at 200ppm. Sanitizer from wall dispenser should not be used until the product is able to be refilled and tested.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Observed wire racks in the fry reach-in freezer to be soiled. Also, observed the cloths stored under clean bowls by salad prep line to be soiled with food splash. Replace cloths nightly. Clean wire racks.  Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.
